findings.intervention: unit-checked target construction, sign convention, monotonicity and decoding in isolation
findings.result: cumulative targets=True; out equals thresholds when g=0=True; higher score lowers P(y<=k)=True; probabilities sum to 1=True; non-negative probabilities=True; expected stage increases with score=True

findings.statement: the ordinal loss has a different scale from cross-entropy
findings.intervention: computed both losses and their head-gradient norms on identical random embeddings
findings.result: loss CE=2.1167 ordinal=3.4664 (ratio 1.64x, ordinal sums 5 BCE terms); head grad norm CE=0.7405 ordinal=2.1052
findings.verdict: SUPPORTED -- ordinal loss is 1.6x CE, so an identical learning rate is not an identical step size

findings.statement: the encoder receives a rank-1 gradient from the ordinal head
findings.intervention: measured the rank and effective rank of dL/d(embedding) for both heads on identical inputs
findings.result: multiclass: numerical rank 5, effective rank 4.89, top singular value holds 26.4%; ordinal: numerical rank 1, effective rank 1.00, top singular value holds 100.0%
findings.verdict: SUPPORTED -- the ordinal gradient is rank-1 while multiclass is higher rank, so the encoder is taught through a single direction

findings.statement: initialisation places the model where gradients vanish
findings.intervention: inspected initial thresholds and the implied class distribution at a zero embedding
findings.verdict: SUPPORTED -- init is strongly biased toward CN, far from the uniform prior, so early gradients fight the initialisation

findings.statement: the head cannot overfit a deliberately learnable subset
findings.intervention: trained both heads to convergence on 12 training-pool subjects (2/class), no dropout, no weight decay, 250 epochs, identical encoder and seed
findings.result: multiclass: train acc 1.00, loss 0.0032, 6 classes predicted; ordinal: train acc 0.67, loss 0.8780, 4 classes predicted
findings.verdict: SUPPORTED -- ordinal cannot memorise even 12 subjects, so this is an optimisation failure, not absent signal
